en: The Triplet on Seeing and the Dyad on Cause.

Dependent on a state that is to be abandoned by seeing (*dassanena pahātabba*) and is a root (*hetu*), there arises a state that is not to be abandoned by seeing and is not a root (*nadassanena pahātabbo nahetu*), by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

(Abbreviated. There are thirteen [modes] under the root condition, nine under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) ... pe ... three under the result condition (*vipāka*) ... pe ... thirteen under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*).
Dependent on a state that is not to be abandoned by seeing and is not a root (*nabhāvanāya pahātabbo nanahetu*), there arises a state that is not to be abandoned by cultivation and is not a root...
It arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the root; nine in the case of the object … pe … three in the case of the result … pe … nine in the case of non-disappearance.
